requirement:
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.

```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
    pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
}
```

The item's span includes its attached source under the language's rules. The
root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. I did not request implementation source. Each test was judged against the requirement text. I found no gaps and no acknowledgments apply.

**Obligation 1: `OutlineContent::outline` exposes the whole retained file's outline, even when the content selects one item.**
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` selects the second line of a three-item outline. It asserts `selected.outline().items.len() == 3`, so the selected value still exposes the whole file's outline. It also selects the root from the selected value and gets the full text `"first\nsecond\n"`.
- `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` asserts `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` for a selected section.
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` makes the same pointer-equality assertion for a selected function.

**Obligation 2: the root is listed first, followed by items in source preorder.**
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts the exact selector list `["", "mod[auth]", "mod[auth]/fn[check]", "mod[auth]/struct[Token]", "fn[last]"]`. It also asserts the kind list `["", "mod", "fn", "struct", "fn"]`. Together these check the root first, parents before nested children, and nested children before the following sibling.
- The Markdown tests assert the ordered section selectors with nested and duplicate (`#1`, `#2`) items. `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` does the same for setext sections.
- `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` and `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` check plain-text line items in source order with their spans.

**Obligation 3: full selectors identify items and their ancestry.**
This is governed by the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, so it needs no test here. The tests still exercise it incidentally. They assert full nested selectors and call `select(selector)` for every item in the Rust and plain-text cases.

**Obligation 4: an item's span includes its attached source under the language's rules.**
- The Rust test asserts that the `fn[check]` span starts at `/// Check tokens.` and contains `#[inline]`. It checks that the span end falls at the end of the function body. It also asserts `selected.text() == &source[item.span]` for every item.
- The Markdown tests check section spans that include their bodies and nested code. For setext sections, the span starts at the title's original source position, including inside directive, quote and list containers.
- Language-specific attachment rules for other languages belong to the per-language `requirements.sdk.sources.*.items` requirements. They are delegated, not assessed here.

**Obligation 5: the root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.**
Root selector `""` and span `Span::new(0, source.len())` are asserted in the Rust, Markdown, plain-text and Unicode tests. They are also asserted for every bundled language in `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline`, both through the public API and through the raw `language.outline` result. The empty-source case asserts a single root item with span `(0, 0)`.

The tests also assert that all item spans are valid slices of the source. They cover non-ASCII byte offsets in the Unicode and Markdown tests.

The item's span includes its attached source under the language's rules. The
root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
